finding.title: Remove dead isShabbos/isYomTov/formatHebrewDate from HebrewCalendarUtils (superseded by zmanim_window_service)
finding.rule: Evans lens (ubiquitous language re-derived, not enforced in one place) + dead code

evidence.quote: /// For precise zmanim (sunset/nightfall), use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation.

finding.why: `grep -rn` across all of lib/ finds zero production callers of isShabbos, isYomTov, or formatHebrewDate outside their own definition file — only test/core/utils/hebrew_calendar_utils_test.dart and one story-acceptance test call isShabbos, testing code nothing else ever runs. Meanwhile lib/features/sacred_time/domain/services/zmanim_window_service.dart implements the real, GeoLocation/zmanim-aware Shabbos+Yom-Tov window (candle-lighting offset, tzais, JewishCalendar.isAssurBemelacha) that actually drives the Sacred Time lock feature — and isShabbos's own doc comment admits its 18:00-local-clock-hour heuristic is inferior ("For precise zmanim... use ComplexZmanimCalendar with a GeoLocation"). Because this dead code lives in core/utils/ (importable by any feature — Rule 1 only blocks core→features, not the reverse) and is unit-tested (making it look supported), a future feature needing "is it Shabbos right now" is one natural-language search away from wiring up the crude, timezone-naive version instead of the correct geo-aware one — and if the caller passes a UTC DateTime (the P5-mandated storage format everywhere else in this codebase), isShabbos's `.hour >= 18` check reads UTC hour, not true local hour, silently wrong for any locale far from UTC.
finding.recommendation: Delete isShabbos, isYomTov, and formatHebrewDate (and their test coverage) from HebrewCalendarUtils. If a lightweight non-geo fallback is genuinely wanted somewhere, rename it to make the approximation explicit (e.g. isApproximateShabbosNoGeo) and doc-link to zmanim_window_service.dart as the source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: `grep -rn "isShabbos\|isYomTov\|formatHebrewDate" learning_tracker/lib/` shows zero references outside sacred_time/ (or the methods are removed entirely).
hebrew_calendar_utils_test.dart's corresponding groups are removed alongside the source methods.

finding.title: Split app_shell_test.dart (1352 lines) and pin_guard_test.dart (646 lines) under the 400-line cap
finding.rule: AG-3 (hand-written Dart files ≤400 lines; checker explicitly scans both lib and test)

evidence.quote: // Unit tests for PinGuard — all onNavigation branches, session helpers,

finding.why: AG-3's own Rule-0 checker command (`find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'`) explicitly includes test/, so these are real violations, not just lib/-scoped ones. app_shell_test.dart is 3.4x the 400-line cap, pin_guard_test.dart 1.6x — both are high quality, non-tautological suites with clear existing group() boundaries (bottom-nav, auth flow, persistent switcher, BUG E3 sub-route switcher, TUT-05 tutor header, FIX#7 contrast, tap-target overlap for app_shell_test.dart; B1-B7/S1-S3/G1-G3 for pin_guard_test.dart) that make splitting mechanical rather than risky.
finding.recommendation: Split app_shell_test.dart along its existing group() sections into e.g. app_shell_navigation_test.dart, app_shell_switcher_test.dart, app_shell_tutor_test.dart, app_shell_contrast_test.dart. Split pin_guard_test.dart into branch-coverage vs session-helper vs fail-safe files.
acceptance_criteria: `find learning_tracker/lib learning_tracker/test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` (AG-3's own checker) shows neither file.

finding.title: Replace date_utils_test.dart's real DateTime.now() read with a fixed/injected clock
finding.why: This is the only wall-clock read across all 14 test files in the batch — every other test in the suite (and in the file's own source, date_utils.dart, which is explicitly designed around a swappable LocalDayClock so "day-boundary semantics are deterministic in tests") uses fixed DateTime.utc(...) literals. Comparing DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() against a freshly-read DateTime.now() with a 1-second tolerance is a live flake source: any CI scheduling jitter, GC pause, or slow VM startup between the two calls pushes the gap over 1 second and fails the test for a reason unrelated to the code under test.
finding.recommendation: Override the LocalDayClock with a fixed fake instant (per the source file's own documented pattern: `localDayClockProvider.overrideWithValue(...)` or `useLocalDayClock`) and assert DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() returns exactly that fixed instant, rather than "close to real time".
acceptance_criteria: The nowUtc test asserts equality against an injected/fixed clock value, not a real-time tolerance window.

finding.title: Inject ParentAnalyticsRepository into RestoreGuard instead of constructing it inline
finding.rule: SM-7 (repositories/services/DAOs constructed only inside their @riverpod provider or a test override)
finding.why: RestoreGuard._resolve() hand-constructs ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl(db) directly inside the navigation-check method rather than receiving it as an injected dependency — a literal SM-7 violation. ParentAnalyticsRepository has no Riverpod provider anywhere in the codebase (it's hand-constructed at 2 more sites outside this batch: local_data_upload_service.dart and device_restore_service.dart), so today nothing lets a test or a future caller swap this repository via ProviderScope; a test that wants to fake it has to fake the whole UserDatabase instead. Real-world cost is low today (the class is a thin, stateless DAO wrapper, and RestoreGuard's closure-based constructor is otherwise a deliberately Riverpod-free, easily-testable design — see its excellent test suite), but if SM-7 ships a checker this line (and its 2 siblings) will need either a wrapping provider or a documented exception.
finding.recommendation: Either add a parentAnalyticsRepositoryProvider (@riverpod, takes UserDatabase) and inject it into RestoreGuard's constructor alongside getDatabase, or explicitly document ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl as an intentional non-Riverpod infra helper exempt from SM-7.
acceptance_criteria: Once SM-7 has a checker, ParentAnalyticsRepositoryImpl( outside core/analytics/ appears only inside a @riverpod provider body, or is allowlisted with a stated reason.

finding.title: Delete the two orphaned .gitkeep files in now-populated guards/ and test/core/utils/ dirs
finding.why: .gitkeep exists solely to keep an otherwise-empty directory tracked by git. lib/core/navigation/guards/ now holds 5 real guard files and test/core/utils/ holds 7 real test files, so both placeholders are vestigial clutter left over from before those directories had content.
